items.title: 4 Legendary REITs With Dividends Built to Weather Every Market Storm
items.summary: Most REITs slashed their dividends when 2008 and 2020 hit hardest, but a stubborn handful kept raising checks straight through both collapses. Four of those survivors are still paying, still growing, and still worth a close look in today's rate environment.

items.title: Lock In Monthly Income: 5 September Strong Buys With High Yields
items.summary: September historically punishes stock investors, and this year the warning signs are louder than usual. Five monthly dividend payers have quietly pulled back to yields that look compelling right now, and Wall Street analysts are taking notice.

items.title: 5 Dividend Stocks That Lose the Most to Taxes When They’re Held Outside of a Roth IRA
items.summary: Some of the highest-yielding dividend stocks on the market carry a hidden cost that erases thousands of dollars every single year, and the bracket you sit in determines just how severe that damage gets.

items.title: Realty Income Corp's Dividend Analysis
items.summary: Realty Income Corp (NYSE:O) recently announced a total dividend of $0.27 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-08-31.  This includes a cash dividend of $0.27 per share, payable on 2026-09-15.  As investors look forward to this upcoming payment, the spotlight also shines on the company's dividend history, yield, and growth rates.

items.title: Monthly Dividends Are the Latest Income Craze, but There Are Risks
items.summary: Stocks and ETFs promising monthly or even weekly income are proliferating, but frequent payouts can obscure volatility and weak total returns.

items.title: How a 79-Year-Old Widow Built a $6,100 Monthly Paycheck Around O, JNJ, and PFF
items.summary: Converting a nest egg into a reliable monthly paycheck sounds straightforward until you realize the yield tier you choose can demand nearly three times as much capital for the same income target. A 79-year-old widow with fixed expenses and no room for error found a middle path most retirees overlook entirely.
